scenarios.title: The Financial Mistake
scenarios.text: An investment you were sure about turns out not to be smart: a restaurant that closed, a fund that froze, a statement you read three times in the car outside the facility.

choices.label: Cut the loss
choices.result: The loss, cut cleanly, and a lesson learned. It stings for a month, and then it becomes a story you tell rookies.

choices.label: Tell {love_interest} everything
choices.result: Everything, at the kitchen table, including the part you were embarrassed about. It's a hard talk and a good one, and you make the next decision together.

choices.label: Bury it in work
choices.result: Work, to forget it: early mornings, long sessions, no thinking. It doesn't quite work, and the statement is still in the glove box.

choices.label: Call the advisor you trust
choices.result: The one advisor who has always told you the truth gets a call that afternoon. You make a plan together, you stick to it, and the hole closes by spring.
choices.lock_text: having learned about money the hard way

scenarios.title: The Family Conversation
scenarios.text: You and {love_interest} talk about starting a family, and neither of you knows the right time.

choices.label: Say now
choices.result: You both say now. It's terrifying and right.

choices.label: Make a plan
choices.result: You make a plan around the contract and the seasons.

choices.label: Wait
choices.result: You agree to wait. The conversation comes back every few months.

scenarios.title: The Family Business
scenarios.text: A cousin wants your money and your name to expand the family store into three towns. The whole family is waiting for your answer, and Thanksgiving is in two weeks.

choices.label: Invest
choices.result: You invest and put your name on the sign. The opening is a family party, and for the first time in years, everyone is in one room.

choices.label: Invest, quietly
choices.result: You put in money but keep your name off the sign. It's safer, and your cousin is a little hurt by the distance.

choices.label: Turn the cousin down
choices.result: No, as kindly and clearly as you can manage. Thanksgiving is quieter this year, and you're sure it was the right answer, mostly.

scenarios.title: The Memorabilia Deal
scenarios.text: A memorabilia collector wants to pay you to sign five hundred footballs in one afternoon, in a hotel ballroom, with a man counting and a camera to prove each one is real.

choices.label: Sign all five hundred
choices.result: Five hundred signatures in one long afternoon. Your hand hurts for days, the check is large, and the man counting never smiles once.

choices.label: Add a hundred for charity
choices.result: All five hundred, plus a hundred extra for the children's hospital auction. The auction raises more than your check, and the collector pays for the extra hundred.

choices.label: Sign for kids at the fence
choices.result: No ballroom, no counting man. You'd rather sign for kids at the practice fence, for free, and you do, every Thursday.

scenarios.title: The Young Kicker's Question
scenarios.text: A college kicker emails you for career advice. It's a long email, carefully written, and the question at the end is a good one: how do you know when to change and when to wait?

choices.label: Write a real answer
choices.result: A long, honest answer, written over two evenings. He prints it out, and two years later he sends you a photo of it taped inside his locker.

choices.label: Call him instead
choices.result: A phone call instead of an email. You talk for an hour, and he sounds exactly like you did at twenty, which is strange and a little moving.

choices.label: Send a short reply
choices.result: A short, kind reply and a 'good luck'. He's grateful, and you wonder later what the longer answer would have been.

scenarios.title: The Retirement Savings
scenarios.text: A financial advisor reviews your long-term plan and asks a question you can't answer: what does your life cost after football, per year, in today's money?

choices.label: Learn the answer
choices.result: The answer, learned over two weeks of spreadsheets, and the next ten questions too. You understand your own money for the first time, and it's calming.

choices.label: Bring {parent} to the next meeting
choices.result: {parent} comes to the next meeting with a legal pad and better questions than yours. You make the plan together, and he insists on paying for lunch.

choices.label: Trust the advisor
choices.result: The advisor knows best, you decide, and stop asking questions. It's easy and restful, and you never learn the number.

scenarios.title: The Public Appearance
scenarios.text: You're invited to a high-profile charity gala in black tie: actors, owners, a senator, a string quartet. You don't own a tuxedo, and the event is Saturday.

choices.label: Go and enjoy it
choices.result: A rented tuxedo, a long night and people you didn't know existed. You enjoy it more than you expected, and someone from a children's charity asks for your number.

choices.label: Go with a purpose
choices.result: A plan, three introductions, and home by eleven. You leave with three useful numbers and a sponsor for your youth camp.

choices.label: Stay home
choices.result: Home, in sweatpants, with takeout and a movie. Nobody at the gala notices except your agent, who sends a single sad emoji at midnight.

scenarios.title: The Family Holiday
scenarios.text: The schedule lands on a family holiday again, the third year in a row. {parent} has already set a place for you at the table, just in case.

choices.label: Bring the holiday to you
choices.result: The whole family, flown in for the weekend. Dinner is in a hotel ballroom, and it's still home, and {sibling} carves the turkey badly.

choices.label: Keep your routine and call
choices.result: Your routine, and a long call between meetings. They put you on speaker at the table, and you hear everyone laughing.

choices.label: Plan a second celebration
choices.result: A second holiday, planned for the bye week, with everything: the dishes, the games, the arguments. Everyone says it's fine. It mostly is.

scenarios.title: The Teammates' Dispute
scenarios.text: Two teammates ask you to settle an argument about who gets the corner locker by the heater. It's been going on for a week, and they both say you're the only fair one.

choices.label: Make them talk it out
choices.result: Both of them, in a room, talking it out in front of you. It takes forty minutes, ends with a handshake, and they decide to share.

choices.label: Pick the right side
choices.result: The right side, after listening to both. One of them sulks for a week, and then admits you were right, grudgingly.

choices.label: Let them settle it
choices.result: Settle it yourselves, you tell them, and walk away. They do, eventually, with a coin flip, some shouting and a handshake.

scenarios.title: The Sponsored Posts
scenarios.text: A company offers to pay for sponsored posts, and the product is fine, mostly.

choices.label: Take the deal
choices.result: You take the deal. The posts do well and feel a little hollow.

choices.label: Test it first
choices.result: You use the product for a month before you post. It's actually good.

choices.label: Decline
choices.result: You decline. Your page stays yours.

scenarios.title: The Long-Term Commitment
scenarios.text: {love_interest} wants to talk about where you'll live after football.

choices.label: Let {love_interest} choose
choices.result: You let {love_interest} choose. It's the right call.

choices.label: Make a list together
choices.result: You make a list together. Your hometown wins.

choices.label: Not yet
choices.result: You say there's time. {love_interest} says there isn't always.

scenarios.title: The Injury Prevention Program
scenarios.text: The club wants you on a new training and recovery program: sleep tracking, cold tubs, a mobility routine at six in the morning. The sports science staff is very excited about it.

choices.label: Follow it to the letter
choices.result: Every piece of it, exactly. Your legs feel younger by October, and the sports science staff starts using your numbers in presentations.

choices.label: Add your own work
choices.result: The program, plus your own work on top. You're stronger and more tired, and the staff worries quietly about the extra load.

choices.label: Do the minimum
choices.result: The minimum: the cold tubs, never the six o'clock mobility. The trainers notice right away, and so, by December, does your hip.

scenarios.title: The Younger Teammate's Mistake
scenarios.text: A rookie makes a mistake: he missed a meeting, then lied about why. He comes to you, not the coaches, white-faced, asking what to do before anyone finds out.

choices.label: Walk him to the coaches
choices.result: Down the hall, together, and you stand beside him while he tells them. It goes better than he feared, and he never lies to a coach again.

choices.label: Listen first
choices.result: Listening first, all of it, and then helping him find the words. He goes in alone, which matters to him.

choices.label: Tell him what you'd do
choices.result: Exactly what you'd do, step by step. He does it, it works, and he thanks you without quite looking at you.
